thought.text:
## Diagnosis

`parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125) reads the whole rest of the line via `_unquoted_value` (`[^\r\n]*`), then strips inline comments with `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part).rstrip()`.

For `KEY= # explanation`, `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) already consumes the space after `=`, so `part` is `"# explanation"`. The regex `\s+#.*` requires whitespace *before* the `#`, which is absent — so nothing is stripped, and the value becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

`KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` correctly stay literal (no preceding whitespace), and quoted values bypass this path entirely, so they're unaffected.

## Change plan

In `parse_unquoted_value`, treat a `#` at the start of the value (position 0) as a comment too, e.g. strip when the value begins with `#` or matches `\s+#`. Minimal edit: change the substitution to also handle a leading `#` (e.g. `re.sub(r"(?:^|\s+)#.*", "", part).rstrip()`), keeping `KEY=#literal` literal by only stripping when the `#` is preceded by whitespace or is the first character after `=` plus optional spaces. Verify against existing tests (lines 90-99) and add cases for `KEY= # c` → `""`, `KEY=#literal` → `"#literal"`, `KEY=a#b` → `"a#b"`.
